reviews.reason: The LXXXIII header on printed page 159 establishes the chapter's beginning. The translation preserves the supplied clauses, but note a is attached to 'now' rather than the disclosure verbs it discusses. Its claim about visionary display goes beyond what the pairing alone establishes.
reviews.suggested_text: And now, my son Methuselah, I will show you all my visions that I have seen before you; I will recount them.[a]
reviews.footnote_changes: Replace note a with: "The source uses both 'show' and 'tell/recount'; both verbs are retained here."

reviews.reason: The principal English clauses are supported, but the notes are incorrectly anchored. The learning alternative belongs with 'learning the book,' and the causal alternative belongs with 'concerning them.' Note d merely repeats the displayed construction.
reviews.suggested_text: I saw two visions before I took a wife, and one of them was not like the other: the first when I was learning the book[a], and the second before I took your mother—I saw a mighty vision[b]; and concerning them[c] I made supplication to the Lord.
reviews.footnote_changes: Retain notes a–c at the corrected anchors. In note b, retain the alternatives 'severe' and 'powerful' but remove the unsupported explanatory flourish about revelation. Delete note d.

reviews.reason: The translation can stand provisionally with the uncertainty about the heavenly disturbance made explicit. The present notes instead attach that uncertainty to Mahalalel, repeat the displayed wording as an alternative, and attach 'I lay down' to the disturbance.
reviews.suggested_text: I was lying down in the house of my grandfather Mahalalel, and I saw in a vision that the heaven was being cleansed and swept away[a], and it fell upon the earth.
reviews.footnote_changes: Replace all existing notes with note a: "The verbs describing the disturbance of heaven are rendered provisionally as 'being cleansed and swept away.' This wording should not be treated as an unambiguous description of the physical action. 'Heaven' may also be rendered 'sky.'"

reviews.reason: Verse 4 begins at the bottom of printed page 159 and continues at the top of page 160 through the trees sinking into the deep. That continuation is present, and no supported clause should be removed. The note anchors are displaced, and 'torn up' should not be presented as equivalent to the displayed severing without qualification.
reviews.suggested_text: And when it fell upon the earth, I saw the earth being swallowed into a great abyss[a], and mountains were suspended upon mountains[b], and hills sank down upon hills, and tall trees were cut off from their trunks[c] and were thrown down and sank into the abyss.
reviews.footnote_changes: Replace note a with: "Or 'a great deep.'" Retain note b at 'mountains were suspended upon mountains.' Replace note c with: "The wording describes severing the trees from their trunks or stock; it does not require the more specific image of uprooting." Delete note d.

reviews.reason: The displayed destruction wording is preferable to the obsolete swallowed-up alternatives. Those notes risk importing the swallowing verb from verse 4. The utterance note is also attached to the wrong phrase.
reviews.suggested_text: And a word fell into my mouth[a] because of it[b], and I lifted up a cry and said, “The earth is destroyed.”
reviews.footnote_changes: Replace note a with: "The source's image, 'a word fell into my mouth,' is retained literally." Replace note b with: "The opening expression is rendered causally here; 'from it' is a more literal alternative." Delete the existing swallowed-up notes c and d. Do not claim an independently established idiom.

reviews.reason: The English preserves the grandfather, raising, reclining beside him, and two questions. However, the supplied source has apparent glyph discrepancies in the grandfather expression and final lament verb; a clean all-glyph acceptance is not justified. The name note is misplaced, and note c omits supported relational and reclining details.
reviews.suggested_text: And my grandfather Malyal[a] lifted me up while I was lying beside him, and he said to me, “Why do you cry out like this, my son, and why do you lament like this?”
reviews.footnote_changes: Replace note a with: "The grandfather's name is spelled differently here from its form in verse 3. 'Malyal' is provisional; the spelling should be checked against the printed line before finalizing the transliteration." Delete notes b and c; neither is needed to preserve the two questions.
reviews.suggested_source_text: Recheck the printed-page-160 verse-6 tokens against the image before release: supplied ወመላእያል፡ and እምሔውየ፡ are not secure diplomatic readings. The final verb appears to read ትአውይ፡ rather than supplied ትአወዩ፡. Do not silently normalize the name to the spelling in verse 3.

reviews.reason: The source does not explicitly supply 'it reveals.' The difficult hidden-sin expression should not be converted into confident disclosure language or treated as an established finite verb meaning 'has hidden.' The final destruction clause does not support the obsolete darkness/gloom notes. The supplied abyss token also appears to contain an extra final letter relative to the printed main text.
reviews.suggested_text: And I told him all the vision that I had seen, and he said to me, “Severe is the sight you have seen, my son, and mighty is the vision of your dream—the hidden things of all the earth’s sin[a]—and the earth is about to sink into the abyss[b] and be destroyed with a great destruction.”
reviews.footnote_changes: Replace note a with: "The hidden-sin phrase is difficult and is retained provisionally as a fragment. The printed wording does not explicitly say 'it reveals'; its grammatical connection with the surrounding clauses remains uncertain. 'The earth' in the following clause makes the understood subject explicit." Replace note b with: "Or 'deep.'" Delete all other existing notes, especially the unsupported darkness/gloom alternatives.
reviews.suggested_source_text: In verse 7, replace ውስተ፡ ቀላይት፡ with ውስተ፡ ቀላይ፡, following the printed main-text reading on page 160; its apparatus reference is note 22. Preserve the asterisk attached to the hidden-sin expression and the asterisk on the following destruction verb.

reviews.reason: The petition is supported, including the final clause as printed, but both existing note anchors are wrong. More importantly, printed page 160 note 30 expressly questions the authenticity of the final clause while allowing accidental omission. That material uncertainty should be disclosed rather than presenting the clause without qualification.
reviews.suggested_text: And now, my son, rise and make your petition to the Lord of glory[a], since you are faithful, that a remnant may remain[b] upon the earth and that he may not wipe out the whole earth.[c]
reviews.footnote_changes: Move the divine-title note to a and the remain/remnant note to b. Add note c: "Charles's apparatus, printed page 160 note 30, calls this final clause's authenticity doubtful because several cited manuscripts omit it, but also allows that it could have been lost through similar endings. It is retained here because it stands in the printed main text." This reports the edition's apparatus, not an independent manuscript examination.

reviews.reason: The displayed English preserves the warning's sense. Note c invents a heavenly son speaking and a new embedded speech, neither warranted by this printed clause. Note a is misplaced and incorrectly frames the actual critical-edition reading as merely an OCR-witness problem.
reviews.suggested_text: My son, from heaven all this[a] will come upon the earth, and upon the earth there will be a great destruction.
reviews.footnote_changes: Replace note a with: "The printed main text has the expression rendered 'all this'; printed page 160 note 32 records variation and omission in the edition's cited witnesses." Delete notes b and c, including the invented alternative speech.

reviews.reason: The prayer, entreaty, request, writing, enduring generations, and address to Methuselah are all present. The supplied disclosure verb differs from the printed form, and 'I showed' should not be secured by that mistranscription. The generations note is attached to 'asked' rather than its subject.
reviews.suggested_text: And after this I arose and prayed and entreated and asked, and I wrote down my prayer for the generations of the world[a]; and I will show you everything, my son Methuselah.
reviews.footnote_changes: Move note a to 'generations of the world'; retain its alternatives about future or enduring generations as provisional renderings. Delete note b, which only restates the disputed past-tense rendering.
reviews.suggested_source_text: Replace አርአየከ፡ with አርእየከ፡, following the printed main text on page 160, with apparatus note 36. Do not conflate the printed reading with the alternatives reported in that note.

reviews.reason: The actual markers establish completeness: verse 11 starts on printed page 160, continues onto page 161, and ends with the shown-path clause immediately before LXXXIV. Thus the chapter contains units 1–11, including both cross-page continuations. The proposed English and notes b–c are adequate as transparent provisional treatment of the corrupt knew/saw/made/built passage and the passive shown-path wording; neither should be certified as unambiguous. However, the supplied source's window expression is not a secure match to the image, so the complete source string cannot yet receive an all-glyph acceptance. The opening 'when' also has a significant apparatus qualification.
reviews.suggested_text: And when I went out below[a] and saw the heaven, and the sun rising in the east, and the moon setting in the west, and a few stars, and the whole earth, and everything as He had known it in the beginning[b], then I blessed the Lord of judgment and extolled Him, because He had brought forth the sun from the windows of the east, and it ascended and rose on the face of the heaven, and set out and followed the path which He showed it.[c]
reviews.footnote_changes: Retain notes b and c, explicitly as reports about the printed edition and provisional English interpretation, not independently checked ancient witnesses. Expand note a to: "The selected main text has 'when' and a spatial term rendered 'below/down'; no geographical setting is specified. Printed page 160 note 38 regards 'when' as a late emendation and proposes an original expression meaning 'thereupon/from there.'"
reviews.suggested_source_text: Recheck and repair እመኅከወ፡ against printed page 161: the image appears to read እመስኮ፡. Keep the dagger on †ዘአመረ፡ and its connection to printed note 12. Retain the entire continuation through ፍኖተ፡ እንተ፡ ተርእየት፡ ሎቱ።; exclude the following LXXXIV header and chapter-84 text. No other source replacement is certified here.
